sources.sweepMetres: Her rower sits 0.69 m forward of her middle and the blade swept at arm's length works some 0.7 m beyond her gunwale, 0.45 + 0.7 m out: 1.34 m from her middle
sources.handsAboveWaterMetres: Her seat lies 0.07 m above her waterline with one aboard (bin/lib/hulls/dugout.py), and a seated man's shoulders stand about 0.6 m over his seat (NASA-STD-3000, sitting shoulder height of a 50th-percentile man, 0.59 m)
sources.sideDrag: A round-bottomed log: the round-bilged hull's cross-flow drag

sources.weight: Her finished hull, 393 L of wood by the model (bin/lib/hulls/dugout.py: a 0.56 m deep, 0.9 m wide, 4.5 m long hull with 5 cm walls, cut from the five logs' square 1 m trunk), in oak
sources.swimmingOffsetY: Drawn at the draft she floats at with one aboard, 0.114 m (bin/lib/hulls/dugout.py): vanilla floats a boat with the water 0.018 m over her selection box's top less this offset
sources.shell: Walls about 5 cm thick, as the Dufuna canoe's (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dufuna_canoe). Carved from one log, a side stands from the bottom with its gunwale free, and a breaker bends it as a cantilever: by the model, 8.6 voxels from the bottom's edge to the gunwale
sources.depthMetres: Keel to gunwale by the model: the 1 m trunk with its top hewn away to a level sheer
sources.waterplaneSquareMetres: So that her 1298 L hold full, with one aboard, brings her gunwale to the water (bin/lib/hulls/physics.py)

sources.charMillimetresPerHour: A burn of 3 to 5 hours chars 6 to 13 mm of wood (Agency House dugout diary, 2021-2023, agencyhouse.org/dugout-canoe)
sources.hollowings: Wet clay goes along the rim before each fire (PHMC dugout project, 2005; SUNY Potsdam, 2015), and the fire is tended round the clock until the clay is spent, about a day and a half: 8.5 cm at a time, the 0.51 m hollow takes six fires and about nine days, as Wampanoag builders burn a mishoon for 6 to 10 days (Plimoth Patuxet, The Making of a Mishoon)
sources.hollowDepthMetres: Rim to floor of the hollow: the 0.56 m hull less its 5 cm bottom
sources.blankDepthMetres: The five logs are a trunk 1 m across: one block, as they lie
sources.blankWaterplaneSquareMetres: The five square logs as they lie, 5 m by 1 m at any draft
sources.unhewnLitres: The square 1 m trunk of five logs, 5000 L, less the finished hull's 1691 L envelope (bin/lib/hulls/dugout.py): hewn away a sixth at each hewing, as the outside is shaped. Shaping it is not timed: the strokes that hew out the char shape the outside with them, a simplification for play until shaping gets work of its own
sources.clay: Wet clay one voxel thick over the rim outline the shape draws (its Clay group), at vanilla's 25 voxels a ball (BEClayForm.PutClay)
sources.axeEdgeMetres: Char has lost its fibres and crumbles, so a stroke breaks it away down to the sound wood along its whole sweep across the hollow, a strip as wide as the axe's edge, about 10 cm on a felling axe
sources.hollowBeamMetres: The hollow's width the stroke sweeps: the hull's 0.9 m beam less its two 5 cm walls (bin/lib/hulls/dugout.py)
sources.wallMetres: Her shell's 5 cm walls: a fire burning with the rim unguarded chars it at the hollow's rate, and once the char reaches through a wall's thickness the blank is spoiled
sources.secondsPerStroke: The best working rhythm with an axe is 25 to 35 strokes a minute (H. Glaser, physiology of forestry work, FAO)
sources.hewSaturation: As hard as a patch of mending: hewing out a day's char by hand

sources.pushNewtons: A sustained two-handed push by an adult, about 300 N (Snook and Ciriello, 1991, maximum acceptable forces)
sources.friction: Wood sliding over wet sand or mud, about 0.4

sources.heave: Balance: 265 kg of log rises slowly to a crest; a light hull rises with it, a heavy one lets it climb the side
sources.capsizeBreakerMetres: Seamanship: a breaking wave as high as an open boat's beam can roll it over
sources.rollResponse: A round-bottomed log has little form stability: tippy in a sea
sources.pitchResponse: A long, heavy log rides through the swell with little pitch

sources.capacityLitres: Her hollow to the rim, by the model (bin/lib/hulls/dugout.py)
sources.deckSquareMetres: Her hollow's opening at the rim catches the rain, by the model (bin/lib/hulls/dugout.py)
sources.drainLitresPerHour: One log, no seams: nothing leaks
